header: How much the TEXT of the query modal grows with its width (step 56b). The modal used to be a fixed 52rem (832 px at the usual 16 px). In step 54i I made it a share of the screen so that the doctors' unit tables do not break, but the text stayed the same size, so on a wide screen it looked small next to the width. Now the text grows with the width and keeps the proportion it had at 52rem (omniScale.css does the sizing; wide tables opt out with the class omni-noscale and keep their size and the room they need).

symbols.name: OMNI_BASE_PX
doc: The old width of the modal in px at a 16 px root: this is the width at which the text proportion was right.

symbols.name: OMNI_MAX_SCALE
doc: I never let the text grow by more than this, however wide the screen: a 1600 px modal would otherwise get 1.9 times the text.

symbols.name: omniScaleFor
symbols.sig: export function omniScaleFor(widthPx: number, basePx: number = OMNI_BASE_PX, max: number = OMNI_MAX_SCALE): number
doc: Returns the factor for a modal that is `widthPx` wide: 1 at the old width or narrower, in proportion to the width above it, capped at OMNI_MAX_SCALE; two decimals.

behaviours: the old width is 52rem = 832 px
at the old width or narrower the text is untouched (1)
it grows in proportion to the width: 1026 px (60% of a 1710 px screen) = 1.23, 1040 px = 1.25
864 px (60% of a 1440 px screen) = 1.04
never more than ${OMNI_MAX_SCALE}, however wide
nonsense gives 1, never NaN
another root size: at 20 px per rem the old width is 1040 px
the crawl reached the tools of the search bar (calculators, converters)
the crawl reached the cards of the modal
a rule for ${c}
a rule for ${c}
a rule for ${c} (and only the sm breakpoint exists in the modal)
a rule for ${c}
no fixed-size leading class (leading-5, leading-[18px]) that would not follow the new font size
no other unit of arbitrary font size that has no rule (px and em are handled: em follows its parent)
the stylesheet scales the root of the modal and lets a table opt out (the variable is 1 inside it)
every size rule multiplies by the variable, with 1 as the fallback (no variable, no change)
the shrink is written ONCE, as 1pt, on the modal's root (change it there)
EVERY font size and line height of the sheet that follows the factor also subtracts the shrink (no size can escape it)
the table that opts out of the growth (omni-noscale) is one point smaller too
the sizes of the factor are untouched: 28 uses of the variable still, none without its fallback
the leading classes come BEFORE the sm: rules, as in Tailwind's own sheet
the modal imports the stylesheet and the factor, computes the factor from the screen (never from the animating box) and sets the variable on the card
the factor is the same at frame 0 and at the end of the unfolding: no ResizeObserver changes it while the box animates
the doctors' table is inside an omni-noscale wrapper (it keeps its size and the room it needs)
...and so is every extra table
